questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wide range of interesting courses, good facilities at the university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The International Office were easy to get in touch with and had organized introductions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard, the housing market is quite tough in Amsterdam

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think you should apply for student housing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course catalogue was easy to navigate, and it was connected to timetables so that I could easily find which courses that would might overlap etc

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I called the international office a couple of times for clarifications

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't take courses that don't correspond with the recommended workload, as the level is quite high

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one course I was very content with - Introduction to Migration Studies. But there was also a course, "Beyond the Surface" which was mostly a chit chat course haha

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It differed, some course was similar, another one was less interactive peer to peer, but had class-based discussions that the professor would facilitate

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Beyond the Surface: Exploring Power, Diversity and Inclusion 
Intoduction to Migration Studies
Environment and International Sustainable Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Migration Studies - although the professor was a bit intimidating at first, I think he managed to create a learning space in which everyone would be extremely well prepared and therefore able to participate in discussions. I don't think I have ever learned so much from one course.

questions.answer: Lost my student card so had to buy a new one

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee, beer and wine is cheap ! groceries probably the same amount. you can get a cinema membership for 18 euros a month and go there as much as you want !!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I went to ballet classes at a place called CREA that is close to my campus. very nice !!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: CREA has a lot of opportunities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Buy a Cineville card, go to museums (student-discount), go to some sport, I also went yoga at a place called Body & Mind which is also attached to the university

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: bike around the city, visit Stedelijk, go to Noord, the sauna, community dinners at De Sering or MKZ

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Hmm easy, as it is a lot like in Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't get any Dutch friends hehe. But I would suggest during group work or if

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Biking !!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) the university has great facilities
2) a lot of nice places with community dinners and events
3) a lot of cultural offers

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting confidence about going to live abroad - I feel like I can do it again, in another country. So definitely getting confidence from overcoming all the bureaucratic stuff, and actually being able to live in a city I don't know, and manage to get a daily life there

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say exams, and balancing your social life and school

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
